title: Synthetic Spider Silk Production on a Laboratory Scale
protocol: Perform PCR using the desired spider silk cDNA and specific primer sets.
Gel-extract and ligate the amplified cDNA into a prokaryotic expression vector, such as pBAD/TOPO ThioFusion.
Transform the ligation products into competent E. coli cells.
Select colonies that contain the recombinant cloning vector and use one colony to inoculate 200 mL of sterile LB supplemented with ampicillin.
Grow this culture overnight by shaking at 200 rpm in an orbital incubator at 37 °C.
Combine the 200 mL of saturated culture with 800 mL of fresh LB culture.
Induce spider silk protein expression for 4 hours by adding 0.2% arabinose (w/v).
Pellet the cells at 16,000x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Add 20 mL of 1x lysis buffer to the 1 L cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet completely in the lysis buffer.
Add lysozyme to a concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Add DNase to digest chromosomal DNA.
Place the sample on an orbital shaker and gently rock for 20 min.
Sonicate the solution at maximum for 1 minute.
Centrifuge the solution at 16,000x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant into a clean 25 mL chromatography column.
Add 1 mL of Ni-NTA slurry (0.5 mL beads) into the column.
Secure the cap and stopcock tightly.
Set the column on a rocker to equilibrate for 1 hour.
Allow the Ni-NTA beads to settle for approximately 2 minutes.
Remove the cap and allow the solution to flow through the stopcock.
Collect the eluted solution for further analysis.
Add 20 mL of 1x wash buffer.
Allow the beads to settle.
Open the stopcock and allow the solution to flow through.
Collect this solution in four 5 mL aliquots for further analysis.
Add 20 mL of 1x elution buffer.
Allow the resin to settle.
Open the stopcock and allow the solution to flow through.
Collect this solution in four 5 mL aliquots for further analysis.
Store samples at 4 °C or -80 °C as needed.
Size-fractionate the samples using SDS-PAGE analysis.
Visualize proteins with silver or Coomassie Brilliant Blue R-250.
Dialyze samples against at least 100 times the sample volume using deionized water for 2 days.
Change the water solution every 6 hours during dialysis.
Weigh six 1.5 mL empty microfuge tubes and record their masses.
Transfer 1 mL of the dialyzed sample into each of the six pre-weighed microfuge tubes.
Flash freeze the samples using liquid nitrogen.
Dry the samples down using a freeze dryer.
Repeat the process of transferring another 1 mL of dialysis sample into each tube until all samples are dried.
Store freeze-dried samples at -80 °C for long-term storage.
Calculate the volume of HFIP needed for each tube to obtain a concentration range from 200 mg/mL to 500 mg/mL or 20% to 50% weight per volume.
Add appropriate amount of HFIP into each tube.
Parafilm the tubes and place on a rocker to solubilize the protein.
Vortex and centrifuge occasionally to facilitate solubilization.
Load at least 25 μl of the solubilized spinning dope into the syringe.
Push the dope vertically to remove all air bubbles from the syringe.
Lock the syringe to the pump.
Raise a beaker filled with 95% isopropanol so the tip of the syringe just breaks the surface.
Set the syringe pump to 15 μl/min and start the program.
Allow the as-spun fiber to sit in the isopropanol for 20 minutes.
Apply double-sided tape to both sides of the comb on the spooling device.
Attach the spooling device to a motor.
Spool the threads at 2 rpm.
Gently grab one end of the fiber with forceps and pull it out of the isopropanol.
Attach the pulled fiber to the edge of one of the comb arms on the spool.
Turn on the motor and guide the fiber onto the spooling device.
Ensure the fiber does not double up or stack during spooling.
Once the entire fiber is spooled, detach the spool from the motor.
Apply glue to the edge of each silk fiber on the double-sided tape.
Attach the spool to the linear actuator.
Record the initial length of the fibers using the caliper.
Lower the spool into a 75% isopropanol bath.
Allow the fibers to equilibrate for 10 minutes.
Set the linear actuator speed to 1.5 mm/sec.
Calculate the final length based on the initial length and desired post-spin draw ratio.
Power the linear actuator for the calculated duration at 1.5 mm/sec.
Slowly raise the spool out of the isopropanol bath after completion.
Allow droplets of isopropanol to dry for 1 minute.
Collect samples for testing.
Mount collected samples on cardstock or foil frames.
Lower the spool back into the 75% isopropanol bath if further post-spin draw ratios are desired.
Allow fibers to equilibrate for 10 minutes before proceeding with additional stretching.
Allow collected samples to equilibrate to standard lab environment conditions for at least 1 hour.
Record humidity and temperature, as they may affect fiber's mechanical properties.
Glue the edges of the cardstock or foil to secure the fiber on the frame.
Take note of the size of the opening of the frame.
Using a light microscope with a 100x or greater magnification, take diameter measurements along the longitudinal fiber axis.
Record at least three measurements.
Secure the frame to a tensometer mechanical loading frame.
Cut the frame on both sides so the tension is only running through the fiber.
Tare the tensometer and collect the data.
Using the data collected and the average diameter, plot a stress strain curve.
Mount the broken fiber on a scanning electron microscope stub for morphological analyses.
Measure the break point diameter using the SEM.
Use the fiber segment away from the break point to estimate and check the initial diameter measured by the light microscope.
Analyze different fractions by SDS-PAGE analysis and visualize proteins with silver or Coomassie Brilliant Blue R-250.
Remove small contaminating proteins through extensive dialysis.
Collect fiber samples from continuous wound fiber on the spool using 25 μL of spinning dope at 20% (w/v).
Determine maximum post spin draw ratios empirically based on recombinant silk protein used for spinning process.
Conduct tensometer tests to analyze mechanical properties of spun fibers.
Analyze spun fibers before or after post spin draw with a scanning electron microscope to visualize ultrastructure.
Use spun fibers for mechanical testing and display results within low variation in post spin draw ratio sample group.
Transform the pBAD TOPO/Thio vector containing the spider silk cDNA into competent E. coli cells.
Inoculate a single colony into 200 mL of LB and grow to saturation overnight.
Add 800 mL of fresh LB after inoculation, then induce expression using arabinose.
Centrifuge the culture at the conclusion of induction to pellet bacterial cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in twenty milliliters of 1x lysis buffer containing DNase.
Place the resuspended cells on an orbital shaker and sonicate to lyse the cells.
Spin the cell lysate in a centrifuge to clear the supernatant of cellular debris.
Collect the supernatant.
Incubate the cell lysate supernatant and Ni-NTA beads in a chromatography column for 1 hour.
Collect the flowthrough after incubation.
Use 20 mL of wash buffer to sequentially wash the column, collecting fractions.
Use 20 mL of elution buffer to sequentially elute proteins from the column, collecting fractions.
Analyze collected fractions by SDS-PAGE.
Transfer pure protein-containing fractions to a dialysis bag.
Dialyze samples against distilled water until completion.
Transfer dialyzed product to pre-weighed centrifuge tubes in 1 mL aliquots.
Flash freeze 1 mL aliquots with liquid nitrogen.
Lyophilize frozen samples.
Add more dialysis sample to dried powder and mix.
Calculate the dry mass of purified protein.
Dissolve dry powder in HFIP to create a 20% (w/v) spinning dope.
Push the spinning dope to the top of the glass syringe column while holding it vertically.
Remove air bubbles from the spinning dope in the syringe.
Attach the loaded syringe to a syringe pump.
Lower the syringe into a 95% isopropanol bath so that the tip barely touches the surface.
Construct a spooling device using a digital caliper with metal combs on both sides.
Apply double-sided tape to each side of the comb for fiber attachment.
Attach the spool to a slow-speed motor using an alligator clip.
Slowly pull the fiber from the alcohol bath and wind it around the spool.
Apply glue to the edge of each fiber segment to secure them in place.
Attach the spooling device to a linear actuator setup using alligator clips.
After post-spin draw, lift the spool from the bath.
Allow isopropanol droplets on the fiber to evaporate before collecting the fiber.
Mount collected fibers on cardstock frames with a 1" x 1" cutout using double-sided tape.
Fix the mounted fibers in place with glue.
Attach the cardstock frame to a tensometer.
Cut the sides of the cardstock frame so that tension runs only through the fiber.
Perform size fractionation of purified recombinant MaSp1 protein fractions using SDS-PAGE analysis.
Visualize the protein fractions with silver staining.
Ensure total protein recovery requires 6 collections for elution samples.
